item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, validates inputs, propagates reader errors, and provides focused multipart and retry tests. Candidate B introduces extensive explicitly forbidden API and behavior changes.","reasons":["A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly with field \"file\" and preserves the requested Upload signature.","A explicitly tests filename/content validation and source-reader failures; B lacks an Upload source-reader failure test.","B adds association options, arbitrary form values, multipart fields, and FilesOption state despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged.","B expands the shared multipart helper and adds substantial seek/close/content-length machinery unrelated to the prescribed buffered Upload path, greatly increasing review and compatibility risk between otherwise passing gates."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, decoding, and errors instead of routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","The RawClient change buffers nearly every unrecognized io.Reader whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even beyond Files.Upload and potentially when retries are otherwise ineffective; this is broader than the contract permits.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a clearly streaming source, although separate RawClient tests exercise an opaque reader."],"risks_b":["Directly violates the frozen contract by adding association fields and changing FilesOption behavior.","Upload calls NewFileWithFields and Raw.Do directly rather than using multipartbody.NewFile and routing through FilesService.Add.","Changes caller-body closing semantics, content length, and retry behavior globally through a custom shared-seeker GetBody implementation; returning the same mutable reader is less idiomatic and riskier than a buffered replay body that creates independent readers-controlled body lifecycle changes may affect existing callers despite passing compatibility gates, and the contract explicitly excludes retry refactoring."]}
